script_clips.voice_text: You rub your palms on a cold morning. That rubbing creates friction between your hands.
Because of that friction, tiny collisions start building. Why do those collisions feel warm?
Those tiny collisions push surface particles faster. Faster particles turn rubbing into rising heat.
Without those faster particles, your hands stay cold. With them, warm hands appear almost immediately.
That means your warm hands are not magic. Your skin is feeling energy spread outward.
